verdict: EOG Resources' profit nearly doubled to $2.8B as oil prices rose about 31% and production grew 10%, lifting total revenue 46% to $8.5B.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue of $8.5B, vs $5.8B a year ago

kpis.label: Production
kpis.note: Thousand barrels of oil equivalent per day — up 10% from 1,301 MBoed a year ago

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: Net cash provided by operating activities, vs $3.1B a year ago

segments.name: Crude oil & condensate
segments.note: Oil produced and sold — 550.4 thousand barrels a day at a composite realized price of $86.72 a barrel, up from $65.95 a year ago. By far the biggest revenue source.

segments.name: Gathering, processing & marketing
segments.note: Fees and sales from gathering, processing and marketing oil and gas — including buying other producers' output and reselling it.

segments.name: Natural gas
segments.note: Natural gas produced and sold, at higher volumes and a composite price of $3.74 per thousand cubic feet, up from $2.80.

segments.name: Natural gas liquids
segments.note: Liquids such as propane and butane separated from natural gas (NGLs) and sold separately.

segments.name: Other revenue & gains
segments.note: Gains on asset dispositions of $242M, mark-to-market derivative gains of $105M and $21M of other net revenue — price-hedge and asset-sale gains, not production sales.

opex.name: Exploration costs
opex.note: Searching for new oil and gas deposits.

opex.name: Dry hole costs
opex.note: Wells that were drilled but did not find producible oil or gas.

opex.name: Impairments
opex.note: Write-downs of the value of some oil and gas properties.

opex.name: Marketing costs
opex.note: The cost of buying oil and gas from others to feed the gathering, processing and marketing business — it rises and falls with that revenue line.

opex.name: Depreciation, depletion & amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of wells and reserves over the oil and gas they produce (DD&A).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, people and overhead.

follow100Note: Segment rows add to $99.99 due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Higher prices, more barrels
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 46% to $8,549M. The composite crude price rose about 31% to $86.72 a barrel and total production rose 10% to 1,433 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day. Crude oil alone brought in $4,392M, up 35%.

takeaways.title: Profit nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Net income rose to $2,781M from $1,471M a year ago, and diluted EPS to $5.33 from $2.70. Operating income was $3,586M on total operating expenses of $4,963M — production costs per barrel stayed controlled even as output grew. Operating cash flow was $3,813M.

takeaways.title: Part of revenue is gains, not sales
takeaways.text: Revenue includes $242M of gains on asset dispositions and $105M of mark-to-market derivative gains — hedging contracts repriced at quarter-end — inside the $368M 'other revenue & gains' line. Those items can swing either way from quarter to quarter, unlike production sales.

oneTimers: Revenue includes $242M of gains on asset dispositions and $105M of net mark-to-market gains on financial commodity and other derivative contracts — both are included in the 'Other revenue & gains' segment line rather than in production sales.
Expenses include $24M of impairments and $29M of dry hole costs.
otherDetail: Other income, net of $45M, less interest expense, net of $67M, gives a net other expense of $22M.
footerNote: Cost of revenue here is production costs as reported on the income statement: lease and well costs ($493M), gathering, processing and transportation costs ($693M) and taxes other than income ($401M) — $1,587M in total. Marketing costs, exploration, dry holes, impairments, depreciation, depletion and amortization and G&A are shown as operating expenses, following the order of the income statement; total costs and expenses were $4,963M.
